newsitem.title: GERMANY: Duisenberg says EMU delay is impossible - paper.
newsitem.headline: Duisenberg says EMU delay is impossible - paper.

text.p: The future head of the European Monetary Institute (EMI), Wim Duisenberg, sees no room in the Maastricht Treaty to allow for a delay to European economic and monetary union (EMU), the German business daily Handelsblatt said on Sunday.

The Dutch central bank governor, who is due to take over from current EMI president Alexandre Lamfalussy on July 1, told the newspaper that any change to the single currency timetable would require a complete renegotiation of the treaty.
A summary of the Handelsblatt report, which is scheduled for publication on Monday, was released ahead of time.
Duisenberg also said any profits resulting from revaluation of European central bank gold reserves should not go to finance ministries but should stay in the possession of central banks.

He added that the EMI this year still had to work out specific rules for the revaluation of gold reserves. These could come into play as soon as the European Central Bank has been established in the spring of 1998, he said.
Duisenberg said those rules would not only apply to reserves that must be transfered to the ECB, but also to those remaining with national central banks.

He added that the when Austrian and Dutch central banks sold and revalued portions of their gold assets, profits had been transfered into reserve accounts. The Bundesbank's gold could be dealt with in a similar way within system of European central banks, he said.
